deities: Ashtabhuja Devi (eight-armed goddess, identified as Mahasaraswati and as Yogmaya, Krishna's sister); Kali, Hanuman and Bhairav (nearby shrines)

history.dynasty: None documented; pilgrim shrine of Puranic legend
history.summary: Hilltop shrine ~3 km west of the Vindhyavasini temple (3.7 km west of Vindhyachal station), the Mahasaraswati point of the Vindhyachal Trikona Parikrama (Vindhyavasini-Mahalakshmi, Kali Khoh-Mahakali, Ashtabhuja-Mahasaraswati). Legend: the infant girl born to Yashoda - Krishna's sister Yogmaya - escaped Kansa's grip and settled on this Vindhya hilltop, appearing eight-armed (Ashtabhuja). The goddess sits in a small rock cave on the hilltop; devotees climb ~100 steps (or now take the Ashtabhuja-Kali Khoh ropeway, eastern UP's first cable car, inaugurated 2021, fare ~Rs 50 return). Nearby are a Bhairav kund and shrines of Kali, Hanuman and Bhairav; the site was historically a tantrik destination for secret poojas/yagyas of kings (verify). The tripadvisor note of a midday closure 1-2 PM is from a single visitor account (verify).

name: Ashtabhuja Devi Temple
town_description: Vindhyachal is a pilgrim town on the Ganga bank in Mirzapur district, eastern Uttar Pradesh, ~8 km west of Mirzapur city and ~70 km from Varanasi. It is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and the hub of the Trikona Parikrama circuit (Vindhyavasini, Kali Khoh, Ashtabhuja); the Vindhya Corridor project is reshaping its temple precinct.

travel.airport: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi (VNS), ~72 km
travel.railway: Vindhyachal railway station, ~3.7 km east (nearest); Mirzapur station ~11 km
travel.road: ~3 km west of the Vindhyavasini temple on the Vindhyachal hillside; hilltop reached via ~100 steps or the Ashtabhuja-Kali Khoh ropeway (~Rs 50 round trip); auto-rickshaws from the main temple (~Rs 200 for the two hill temples)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri (crowded); weekday mornings
